title: CloudPipe — Cost Overview
description: Pipeline spend per participant and per component, from Kubecost allocation data. Figures settle over about three days — read the dashboard notes before quoting a number.

panels.title: Read this before quoting a number

options.content:
### 💰 What the pipeline costs

Spend is attributed per participant by tagging every pod with the subject it is processing, then reading Kubecost's allocation data once a day.

**Unit cost is per _run_, not per person.** One workflow = one participant processed once. Test batches reuse a fixed subject list, so the same people are reprocessed constantly — over the 30 days to 2026-08-09, 317 runs covered just 100 participants. Dividing spend by distinct participants would have reported $0.85 where the real unit cost was $0.27, so these panels divide by distinct workflows instead.

**⚠️ Recent numbers are too high.** Cloud billing reconciles over roughly three days as reserved-capacity and spot discounts are applied. A figure scraped the day after a run has historically overstated the settled cost by a **median of ~51%** — occasionally much more. Numbers older than three days are reconciled and trustworthy; the last two days are provisional.

**Component costs are list price.** The CPU/memory/GPU split is *gross* — it does not carry the discounts that land later, which is why the components can add up to more than the reconciled total.

**Rows without a participant are probe runs** — infrastructure warm-ups, not real work — and are excluded from the per-participant figures.

panels.title: Total spend

targets.rawSQL: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total_cost_usd), 2) AS total_cost FROM cloudpipe_metrics.costs WHERE CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo())

panels.description: Sum over every cost record in range, including probe runs and reprocessing. This is the money actually spent, not a per-participant estimate.

panels.title: Runs / participants

targets.rawSQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name) AS runs, COUNT(DISTINCT subject) AS participants FROM cloudpipe_metrics.costs WHERE CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND subject IS NOT NULL AND subject <> ''

panels.description: `runs` = distinct workflows with attributed cost in range — one workflow is one participant processed once. `participants` = distinct people behind those runs. The two diverge whenever a subject is reprocessed, which is routine here because test batches reuse a fixed subject list; over a typical month `runs` has been ~3x `participants`. Probe runs (no subject tag) are excluded from both.

panels.title: Cost per run

targets.rawSQL: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total_cost_usd) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name), 0), 3) AS mean_cost FROM cloudpipe_metrics.costs WHERE CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND subject IS NOT NULL AND subject <> ''

panels.description: Total spend divided by distinct workflows — the cost of processing one participant once. Two traps this avoids: it is NOT an average of per-row costs (rows are per workflow per scrape-date, so a run spanning midnight UTC contributes several rows), and it does NOT divide by distinct participants, which inflates the figure by the reprocessing multiple — with a fixed test-batch subject list that ran ~3.2x over the 30 days to 2026-08-09, turning a true $0.27 into $0.85. The July 2026 rightsizing is often quoted as taking this from $0.74 to $0.36; that pair came from day+1 scrapes, and on the settled re-scrape of the same 2026-07-31 A/B it reads $0.379 -> $0.304 per run. Even that is soft — the two cohorts share only 2 of 10 subjects, and per-POD cost is flat between them ($0.0212 vs $0.0208), so most of the gap is BOLD run count, not rightsizing.

panels.title: Daily spend

targets.rawSQL: SELECT CAST(date AS TIMESTAMP) AS time, ROUND(SUM(total_cost_usd), 2) AS daily_cost, ROUND(SUM(cpu_cost_usd), 2) AS cpu_cost, ROUND(SUM(memory_cost_usd), 2) AS memory_cost FROM cloudpipe_metrics.costs WHERE CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 ASC

panels.description: Total, CPU, and memory cost per day. Expect the most recent one or two points to fall as billing reconciles.

panels.title: Cost per run, by component
panels.description: Where the money goes: CPU, memory, GPU. Per workflow run, matching the `Cost per run` stat. Gross list price, as described in the notes — use it to compare components against each other, not to reconcile against the billed total.

targets.rawSQL: SELECT ROUND(SUM(gpu_cost_usd) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name), 0), 4) AS "GPU (gross)", ROUND(SUM(gpu_cost_usd) * (SUM(total_cost_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(cpu_cost_usd + memory_cost_usd + gpu_cost_usd), 0)) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name), 0), 4) AS "GPU (net)", ROUND(SUM(cpu_cost_usd) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name), 0), 4) AS "CPU (gross)", ROUND(SUM(cpu_cost_usd) * (SUM(total_cost_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(cpu_cost_usd + memory_cost_usd + gpu_cost_usd), 0)) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name), 0), 4) AS "CPU (net)", ROUND(SUM(memory_cost_usd) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name), 0), 4) AS "Memory (gross)", ROUND(SUM(memory_cost_usd) * (SUM(total_cost_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(cpu_cost_usd + memory_cost_usd + gpu_cost_usd), 0)) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name), 0), 4) AS "Memory (net)" FROM cloudpipe_metrics.costs WHERE CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND subject IS NOT NULL AND subject <> ''

panels.title: Spend by participant
panels.description: Top 50 by total cost, summed over every time the participant was processed. `runs` counts the distinct workflows — divide `total_cost` by it to get the per-run cost. `days` counts the distinct scrape dates the participant appears on; it can exceed `runs` when a single run spanned midnight UTC.

targets.rawSQL: SELECT subject, ROUND(SUM(total_cost_usd), 2) AS total_cost, ROUND(SUM(cpu_cost_usd), 2) AS cpu_cost, ROUND(SUM(memory_cost_usd), 2) AS memory_cost, COUNT(DISTINCT workflow_name) AS runs, COUNT(DISTINCT date) AS days FROM cloudpipe_metrics.costs WHERE CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE($__timeFrom()) AND DATE($__timeTo()) GROUP BY subject ORDER BY total_cost DESC LIMIT 50
